title: Praise Ye the Lord, Exalt His Name
description: Praise Ye the Lord, Exalt His Name in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 135, part 1, headed “The church is God's house and care”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Praise ye the Lord, ex-alt his Name, While in his ho-ly courts ye wait, Ye saints, that to his house be-long, Or stand at-tend-ing at his gate.

lines: Praise ye the Lord, exalt his Name,
While in his holy courts ye wait,
Ye saints, that to his house belong,
Or stand attending at his gate.
Praise ye the Lord; the Lord is good;
To praise his Name is sweet employ;
Israel he chose of old, and still
His church is his peculiar joy.
The Lord himself will judge his saints;
He treats his servants as his friends;
And when he hears their sore complaints,
Repents the sorrows that he sends.
Thro' every age the Lord declares
His Name and breaks th' oppressor's rod;
He gives his suffering servants rest,
And will be known th' almighty God.
Bless ye the Lord, who taste his love,
People and priests exalt his Name:
Amongst his saints he ever dwells;
His church is his Jerusalem.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
